sections.h2: Where does Toombs County sit, and what towns does it hold?
sections.html:
Toombs County is in southeast Georgia, with Lyons holding the courthouse and Vidalia ranking as the biggest city. State lawmakers established it on August 18, 1905, as Georgia's 144th county and it organized that October, per Wikipedia.

Land came from Tattnall and Montgomery counties, and a sliver of Emanuel County joined in 1907 to complete today's outline. Total area is 371 square miles. South of Vidalia the water flows to the Altamaha River, and the northern half around Lyons feeds the Ohoopee River.

The cities are Lyons, Santa Claus and Vidalia, and Ohoopee is a census-designated place. Center, English Eddy, Normantown and South Thompson are among the unincorporated communities. Emanuel, Candler, Tattnall, Appling, Jeff Davis, Montgomery and Treutlen counties touch its borders. The county sits within the Vidalia micropolitan area, and the Toombs County School District runs its public schools.

sections.h2: How affordable are Toombs County homes?
sections.html:
Toombs has the cheapest houses of the four counties in this group. The Census Bureau's 2020-2024 median is $137,000, and owners occupy 60.5% of units.

The county recorded just 35 building permits for 2025, so nearly every sale involves an existing house. The 2020 census tallied 10,505 households among 12,027 housing units, 12.7% of them empty, with 9.5% of rentals vacant. The mid-2025 population estimate is 27,545, a 1.9% rise over the 2020 base. The poverty rate is 22.8%, which tops the four counties, and 16.3% of people under 65 have no health insurance.

sections.h2: Who sends the bill and who sets the value in Toombs County?
sections.html:
Billing and collection sit with the commissioner, whose office is at 100 Courthouse Square, Suite 169, Lyons, GA 30436. Call (912) 526-8575. Doors open at half past eight on weekdays and close at half past four.

The county tax site's FAQ gives (912) 526-6291 for the assessors, who determine value and take returns and exemption forms. A copy of a warranty deed comes from the courthouse deed room, which the superior court clerk runs.

  • Commissioner: statements, payments, mobile home decals, delinquent sales
  • Assessors: valuation, returns, homestead filings, first-level appeals
  • Board of Equalization: named by the Grand Jury, hears value disputes
  • County commissioners and school board: adopt the millage rates

The county site makes clear that the commissioner does not decide value or rates. A complaint about the size of the bill belongs with the elected boards that levy it.

sections.h2: When does Toombs County tax come due, and what happens after?
sections.html:
Two county pages give two answers. One says statements are mailed by October 20 with payment due December 20. The FAQ says real estate and business personal property have been due November 15 since 2018.

Trust the date on your own statement, and phone (912) 526-8575 if it looks off. After the deadline the FAQ charges interest of 1% monthly, plus a 10% penalty on tax still open 90 days out. Once a bill sits unpaid past 30 days, a lien known as a fi. fa. can be recorded. These records are public, and the FAQ warns that credit bureaus may see them.

  • Interest on real estate: 1% per month
  • Penalty at 90 days: 10%
  • Lien: can be recorded after 30 days unpaid
  • Mobile homes: April 1 deadline, then 10% plus 1% monthly

The tax sales page announced an auction for December 2, 2025, at 10 a.m. on the courthouse steps, and that date is behind us. The sale list can be viewed at the office, where staff can give the next date.

sections.h2: What should a Toombs County seller do about unpaid tax?
sections.html:
Ask the commissioner for a written balance on the parcel before you sign anything. Georgia's revenue department says no refund exists for a part year, which leaves the January 1 owner with the entire amount.

Lyons, Santa Claus and Vidalia are cities, and a home inside one may owe city tax along with county tax. Ask whether both apply. If you have fallen behind, check the clerk's records for a recorded lien too, since a title company will want it released. When the roof, wiring or plumbing needs money you lack, an as-is cash buyer removes the repair bill, and any tax owed comes out of the price at closing.

A clear payoff letter and a copy of the recorded deed are the two papers that move a closing fastest.

sections.h2: Does a Toombs County owner have to file a property return?
sections.html:
Georgia law treats everything owned and taxable on January 1 as property to be returned to the assessors between January 1 and April 1, the county's general information page says. An owner who files nothing is treated as having returned the same property at last year's final value, with the same real estate exemptions.

The FAQ explains that an owner who thinks the value is too high can file a return stating their own opinion of market value. That filing is what creates appeal rights if the assessors change the number again. Returns for real estate go to the assessors, and the FAQ lists real property, personal property, motor vehicle, mobile home and timber among the taxes the commissioner bills.

  • Return window: January 1 through April 1
  • No return filed: last year's value and exemptions carry over
  • Own-value return: starts the appeal path if the assessors disagree

Household goods are not normally taxable, per the same FAQ, so a seller does not owe tax on furniture left in the house.

sections.h2: Which homestead amounts appear on the Toombs County site?
sections.html:
The county's information page lists amounts for its regular exemption, for owners who live in the house before January 1. It shows $20,000 off assessed value for county operations, $2,000 off county school tax and $2,000 off the state share. A house inside a city also gets $10,000 off the city and city school tax.

Further categories carry labels: S3 for age 62 and up with an income test, S4 and SC for age 65 and up, S5 for disabled veterans, SS for unremarried surviving spouses, and a local school-tax exemption at 70 and over. The 62-and-over school exemption uses a $10,000 earned-income limit for the prior year. Because details vary by category, ask the assessors which one fits your situation.

Forms are taken from January 1 through April 1, and the page adds that state law allows no extension. After approval the exemption renews on its own until eligibility changes. A move requires a new application for the new address.

sections.h2: What are the steps to challenge a Toombs County assessment?
sections.html:
Send a letter to the Toombs County assessors, with 45 days counted from the date on the notice. The county site says notices tend to arrive in spring.

Valid grounds are taxability, value, uniformity or a refused exemption. You choose one of three tracks, which are the equalization board, a hearing officer, or arbitration, and a case can carry on to Superior Court after that. Mobile homes follow their own clock. The county says a different value can be declared within 45 days of the bill mailing, and a change notice allows a further appeal to the Board of Equalization inside 21 days.

faqs.q: How do I contact the Toombs County tax commissioner?
faqs.a: Phone (912) 526-8575 or stop by 100 Courthouse Square, Suite 169, in Lyons. The office is open weekdays from half past eight to half past four.

faqs.q: Does Toombs County tax come due in November or December?
faqs.a: The county's pages conflict: one cites December 20 and the FAQ cites November 15. Use the date on your bill and double-check with the commissioner's office.

faqs.q: What does paying Toombs County tax late cost?
faqs.a: Interest accrues at 1% a month after the deadline, and a 10% penalty hits tax still unpaid 90 days later. A lien may be filed with the superior court clerk once 30 days pass.

faqs.q: When are Toombs County mobile home taxes due?
faqs.a: Each April 1. Later payments draw a 10% filing penalty and a 1% monthly charge, and the owner gets a location permit and decal only after paying in full.

faqs.q: How long does an owner have to dispute a Toombs County value?
faqs.a: The window is 45 days from the date on the assessment notice. Put the dispute in writing to the assessors and say which route you want: equalization board, hearing officer or arbitrator.
